title: OpenAI's ring-shaped smart speaker will reportedly cost between $300 and $400
excerpt: OpenAI's first hardware device is a ring/doughnut-shaped, hockey-puck-sized screenless smart speaker designed with Jony Ive, priced at $300-$400. It is battery-powered and portable, with a camera and sensors feeding it context about its environment.
rationale: The first hard spec and price for the Jony Ive OpenAI device — a screenless, sensor-fed object that forces designers to think about interaction without a display.

title: Meta Ray-Ban smart glasses are getting smarter with a significant AI model upgrade
excerpt: Meta's v127 update brings the Muse Spark model to Ray-Ban Display, plus Neural Handwriting — writing prompts with a finger on any flat surface via the Neural Band — and Threads/Instagram voice interactions.
rationale: Neural Handwriting turns any flat surface into an input field — a genuinely new text-entry modality shipping on consumer eyewear today.

title: iOS 27 basically turns your iPhone and AirPods into an Apple Watch at the gym
excerpt: iOS 27 extends GymKit beyond the Apple Watch, letting iPhone plus AirPods Pro 3 tap gym equipment for real-time metrics — sensing moves off the wrist and into the ears.
rationale: Sensing moves off the wrist and into the ears — a concrete signal that health UX should stop assuming a watch is the primary sensor.

title: Viture's New XR Glasses Are Sharper, Brighter, and Way Less Expensive
excerpt: Viture's Pro 2 XR glasses drop to $299 while getting sharper, brighter and roughly 20% lighter than the previous generation — pushing wearable displays toward everyday price and comfort.
rationale: A $299, 20%-lighter wearable display moves head-mounted screens into everyday territory — the price point where designing for glasses stops being speculative.

title: I hope Galaxy Z Flip 8 isn't the last of its kind, but I can see why it might
excerpt: The Z Flip 8's redesigned FlexWindow brings Gemini Intelligence and Now Brief to the cover screen, but app restrictions limit how far the glanceable, unfold-free AI interaction model actually goes.
rationale: A shipping case study in glanceable AI on a tiny cover screen, and exactly where platform restrictions break the unfold-free interaction model.
